title: Agent Workbench Engineering: Why Capable Models Still Fail

questions.question: What does the lesson identify as the root cause of agent failures on real tasks?
options: Insufficient model parameters compared to a larger frontier checkpoint from the same vendor
Slow network latency between the agent runtime and the model provider's API endpoint
Workbench failures: missing surfaces around the model, not LLM limitations
Outdated training data that predates the repository's current dependency versions
questions.explanation: The model is not wrong about Python; it is wrong about the work. Surfaces around the model are missing.

questions.question: What are the seven workbench surfaces the lesson names?
options: Train, eval, deploy, monitor, retrain, scale, and retire model versions across releases
Plan, act, reflect, refine, debate, vote, and ship as a multi-agent consensus loop
Read, write, exec, fork, exit, wait, and kill as POSIX process primitives
Instructions, state, scope, feedback, verification, review, handoff
questions.explanation: The seven surfaces are instructions, state, scope, feedback, verification, review, handoff.

questions.question: Which is NOT one of the eight distributed-systems primitives the lesson maps surfaces to?
options: Backpropagation
Function primitive
Worker primitive
Trigger primitive
questions.explanation: The eight primitives are function, worker, trigger, runtime, HTTP/RPC, queue, session persistence, authorization policy.

questions.question: What did Vercel's reported harness change move success rate from and to?
options: 20% to 60%, by adding a second reviewer worker to the pipeline
80% to 100%, by deleting 80% of the agent's tools
0% to 100%, by switching to Claude Opus with more parameters
50% to 70%, by adding retrieval-augmented generation
questions.explanation: Deleting 80% of tools moved Vercel's agent from 80% to 100% success.

questions.question: What does Terminal Bench 2.0 demonstrate about model vs harness?
options: Models alone determine ranking regardless of tool count or harness configuration used
Harness changes do not matter once the underlying model has enough training data
Same model moved from outside top 30 to rank five by changing only the harness
Only GPU throughput and inference speed determine an agent's benchmark ranking
questions.explanation: LangChain's Anatomy of an Agent Harness: same model, harness change, 25+ rank jump.

questions.question: What does the lesson recommend doing when you hear new harness vocabulary?
options: Adopt the vocabulary verbatim from whichever vendor, blog post, or conference talk introduced the new harness term this quarter
Reject any new vocabulary outright and continue using only the original agent-loop terminology forever
Wait for OpenAI to standardize the vocabulary across every vendor before using any harness term at all
Translate back to primitives (function, worker, trigger, runtime, HTTP/RPC, queue, persistence, policy) before adopting
questions.explanation: Reason from primitives, not vendor taxonomies; the vocabulary changes but the engineering does not.

questions.question: Where does chat history sit relative to the workbench?
options: Chat is volatile; the repo is the system of record
Chat is the system of record; the repo just mirrors it
Both are equivalent; the repo regenerates from chat
Neither matters; the model re-derives context alone
questions.explanation: The loop closes on the state file, not on chat history.
